subject: FY 2023 Budget Review
overview: The Committee reviewed the FY 2023 budget proposals for several departments and debated the causes of an $8 million revenue shortfall. The Council expressed severe dissatisfaction with the administration regarding the lack of a formal budget book and the legal compliance of specific personnel salary grades.

items.title: Human Resources
items.summary: Director Neil Osborne discussed the department's transition to a standalone entity, while Councilors raised concerns regarding the legal validity of the director's current salary classification.

items.title: Council on Aging
items.summary: Director Pam Kelly reviewed senior services, nutrition programs, and the department's reliance on federal and state grant funding for operational extras.

items.title: Planning, Development, and Sustainability
items.summary: Director Alicia Hunt outlined implementation plans for the Climate Action Plan and park renovations, while the Council emphasized the need for a zoning consultant to unlock commercial revenue.

items.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
items.summary: Director Frances Nwajei presented her department's mission and highlighted language access and ADA compliance as critical immediate needs for the city.

items.title: Commissions and Boards
items.summary: The Committee reviewed level-funded budgets for the Board of Appeals and Community Development Board, while tabling the Historic Commission budget for further review.

items.title: Legislative Budget Schedule
items.summary: Approved a motion to move the Legislative budget to the end of the hearing schedule to ensure a direct discussion with the Mayor regarding Council priorities.

items.title: Budget Process and Shortfall Discussion
items.summary: The Council debated the administration's delay in providing budget documentation and the impact of revised ARPA revenue calculations on the city's $8 million deficit.
